title: Swift v. Tyson (1842)
summary: The historical Swift approach allowed the federal court to decide a general commercial-law question independently of state judicial precedent.
notes: The course assigns Swift through the discussion in Erie. It is historical and superseded in its general-common-law approach; its commercial setting does not authorize modern federal courts to invent general contract law.

sections.Parties: Swift sought payment on a negotiable instrument involving Tyson. The underlying transaction and transfer raised questions about fraud and value given for the instrument.
sections.Material Facts: The disputed issue concerned whether a holder who took the instrument in connection with a preexisting debt could claim the protection afforded to a holder for value. State decisional law supplied one approach. The federal court classified the matter as a general commercial-law question rather than a local statutory rule.
sections.Procedural History: The Supreme Court adopted the independent general-law approach under its reading of the Rules of Decision Act. Erie later overruled that approach.
sections.Issue: Did the Act require the federal court to follow the state courts’ view of a general commercial-law issue?
sections.Holding: Under Swift’s historical construction, no. The court could develop its own understanding of general commercial law.
sections.Reasoning: The opinion treated the relevant state judicial decisions as evidence of general law, rather than conclusive statements of a state-created rule. It anticipated the development of uniform commercial principles through independent judicial reasoning. Erie later criticized both the statutory interpretation and the practical consequences, including divergent law and strategic forum selection.

learning.why: The historical Swift approach allowed the federal court to decide a general commercial-law question independently of state judicial precedent.

topics.cp-erie-history: Swift permitted an independent federal general commercial law later rejected by Erie.
topics.cp-precedent: The opinion distinguished state statutes and local law from state judicial views on general commercial questions.

mnemonic.rationale: A bill of exchange and general common law
